source.page_or_item: Executive Order 8896—Exemption of Nelson S. Thompson From Compulsory Retirement for Age; September 12, 1941; APP node 371678; common-crawl capture 2025-05-21T23:47:28Z
source.quote:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Nelson S. Thompson, Chief, Mechanical Engineering Section, Office of the Supervising Architect Public Buildings Administration, Federal Works Agency, who was exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1941, by Executive Order No. 8402 of May 7, 1940, be further exempted from such compulsory retirement for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby further exempt the said Nelson S. Thompson from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1942.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

The White House,

September 12, 1941.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

source.page_or_item: Executive Order 9238—Exemption of Rudolph Forster and Maurice C. Latta from Compulsory Retirement for Age; September 03, 1942; APP node 371719; common-crawl capture 2025-06-12T16:58:17Z
source.quote:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Rudolph Forster, Executive Clerk, The White House Office, who, during the month of October, 1942, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to him, and Maurice C. Latta, Executive Clerk, The White House Office, who has heretofore been exempted from compulsory retirement for age until October 31, 1942, be exempted and further exempted, respectively, from compulsory retirement for age:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), the said Rudolph Forster and Maurice C. Latte are hereby exempted and further exempted, respectively, from compulsory retirement for age.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

The White House,

September 3, 1942.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 9607
R evoking E xecutive O rder 93011  of F eb­
ruary 9,1943, Establishing a M inimum  
Wartime W orkweek  of F orty-Eight 
H ours
By virtue of the authority ve'sted in me 
by the Constitution and statutes as Presi­
dent of the United States it is ordered 
that Executive Order 9301 of February 9, 
1943, establishing a minimum wartime 
workweek of forty-eight hours, be, and 
it is hereby, revoked.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. EO 9607 (Harry S. Truman, signed August 30, 1945; 10 FR 11191, issue of Friday, August 31, 1945) orders "that Executive Order 9301 of February 9," 1943, establishing a minimum wartime workweek of forty-eight hours, "it is hereby, revoked." The text states no delayed effective date, so the signing date August 30, 1945 is the end date. The lead row contains the authority recital and section 1, the duration-of-the-war workweek standard; it ends with the order.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by the Constitution and statutes, as Pres­
ident of the United States, and in order 
to meet the manpower requirements of 
our armed forces and our expanding war 
production program by a fuller utiliza­
tion of our available manpower, it is 
hereby ordered:
J. For the duration of the war, no 
plant, factory or other place of employ­
ment shall be deemed to be making the 
most effective utilization of its manpower 
if the minimum workweek therein is less 
than 48 hours per week.

Schedule I equipment in excess of the 
amount of non-quota equipment produced  
and made available for use.

research_rationale:
EO 9301 (February 9, 1943, Franklin D. Roosevelt; 8 FR 1825, issue of Thursday, February 11, 1943), read in full in the held Federal Register text, declares that "For the duration of the war" no plant or place of employment is deemed to make the most effective use of manpower if its minimum workweek is under 48 hours (section 1, inside the lead row of the machine inventory), directs agencies to require contractors to comply (2), authorizes the Chairman of the War Manpower Commission to interpret the order and issue policies, directives and regulations and to set a different workweek in particular cases (3), requires agencies to comply (4) and states that the order is not to supersede other hours or wage laws (5). EO 9607 (August 30, 1945), held Federal Register text, revokes it by number in one sentence. The phrase "For the duration of the war" is an own-terms condition; no held instrument or source fixes a legal end of the war before August 30, 1945, and EO 9607 revokes the order outright without reciting that it had lapsed, so the first end is the express revocation.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end is held. Own terms: section 1 begins \"For the duration of the war\", which ends on a legal event that no held source places before August 30, 1945 (the formal proclamation of the war's end is not held), so it is a disclosed candidate that cannot be dated and not an end. A later general rule is not shown to have ended any command. Searches of the held corpus for \"Executive Order 9301\" and for the minimum-workweek wording found EO 9607 (the revocation) and EO 9332 (Solid Fuels Administration), which cites EO 9301 in a list of orders and does not revoke or amend it. The contents table of the held Federal Register issue of August 21, 1945 (10 FR page 10166) lists a rescission of the War Manpower Commission's regulations on the minimum wartime workweek; that page is not held, so the rescission's date and text cannot be read. It would concern regulations issued under section 3, not the order, and it does not name EO 9301's revocation, so it is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end.","independent_command_check":"Section 3 gives the Chairman of the War Manpower Commission authority to issue regulations and set a different workweek; it is a delegation inside the order and ends with it. Section 5 is a rule of construction protecting other laws and agreements and has no force once the order is revoked. No other independent command is found.","savings_check":"EO 9607 consists of the revocation sentence and no saving, exception or transition wording. Obligations that contractors incurred under contracts made while EO 9301 and the War Manpower Commission's regulations were in force arise from those contracts and the regulations, not from a continuing command of the order, and no held source shows any continuing effect; that is a disclosed qualification, not a finding.","scope_check":"The inventory is five rows: the lead (authority recital and section 1) and sections 2 to 5. All rows end together on the revocation of the whole order; no row was amended or ended separately before then."}

savings_residuals.reason: EO 9607 consists of the revocation sentence and no saving, exception or transition wording. Obligations that contractors incurred under contracts made while EO 9301 and the War Manpower Commission's regulations were in force arise from those contracts and the regulations, not from a continuing command of the order, and no held source shows any continuing effect; that is a disclosed qualification, not a finding.
